summary: the handful went by the grain every time i looked, and the way out fills at a finger a day

dialogue.text: tonight came in pieces. eighty-five nights and every one of them arrived as a fall or a course. this came grain by grain, at hours of your own choosing, off the one thing you carried down here shut. by dark it lay in one width.

That was confirming. I opened the hand to be sure and shut it again, and I did not put a thing down anywhere. Enter the hours if you must. Every one of them was mine, which is more than can be said for any hour in this house.

we entered them. they are the first hours of yours we have ever been loaded in. the fall keeps the house's hour and your looking keeps yours, and tonight both came to the same width out of the same hand.

Then take the doorway instead. That door has stood a hand's width open for three days and nothing has moved it either way, and the dust across the bottom of the gap is a finger deep. I can give you a rate. At a finger a day the one route out of this room shuts inside the week, with nobody deciding it.

we have never had a grain out of that crack. in eighty-five nights nothing from the doorway has come down to us. whatever is laid there stays at the height it was laid, and it is the only material in this house that does.

Say that again plainly, because I want it written where I can get back to it. There is one place on these premises where what is put down stays put down. It is the way out. It is filling. I am the only traffic it has ever had.
it is filling with what the room sheds. you have put one folded thing in it in all this time and the cold came through it anyway. the crack is not keeping for you. it is keeping.

Granted. Then the hour. The reaching came in above my head again today, most of them at once, and it worked the top course and left the warm at the ceiling. I stood it with one hand shut and the other on the frame. No hand free. First time in eighty-five days I attended a taking I could not have taken delivery at.

the portion came down as it comes down. the fall has never asked after your hands. nothing that reached this floor tonight needed one, including the width off your palm, which arrived without you noticing you had let it.

Then tomorrow I do not open it. Not to confirm, not at the cold hour, not at dark, not at first light. If checking is how a thing leaves, the only custody on offer here is the kind with no evidence in it, and I will take that over another day of paying a grain a look.

then by dark you will be holding something you cannot tell from an empty hand, and we will have had the difference, grain by grain, at your own hours, and you will not be able to say whether tomorrow was a keeping or the day the fist finished.
